subject: SLA template - exception coverage & monthly credit limits
messages:
From: Maya Rao <maya@edgewave.com>
To: avery_johnson@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@edgewave.com
Date: 2026-08-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SLA template - asking for higher uptime and credit cap

Hi Avery,

Thanks for taking this back to the team. As part of our procurement review we wanted to propose two changes to Redwood's standard SLA template for the Edgewave contract:

1) Uptime target: we need the standard availability threshold to be 99.95% (monthly). Our compliance and customer obligations require this floor.
2) Monthly service credits: we propose a linear credit formula up to a cap of 50% of the monthly invoice for availability shortfalls below 99.95%.

We understand this is above your standard offering — our acceptance of production data residency + a 12-month commit is conditional on these terms.

Can you confirm what trade-offs Redwood would need (commit level, dedicated capacity, maintenance carveouts) to meet 99.95 and the 50% cap? I'm attaching a short note from Edgewave procurement that explains the internal requirement (Edgewave-SLA-ask-20260816.pdf).

Also: we expect maintenance windows not to be more than 4 hours/month and would like a clear formula for how credits are calculated (and when they are paid out).

Thanks,
Maya
Procurement, Edgewave Systems

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Maya Rao <maya@edgewave.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-16T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA template - asking for higher uptime and credit cap

Hi Maya —

Appreciate the clear ask and the context. Quick summary from our side after an initial review:

- Redwood standard hosted SLA is 99.9% monthly availability with credits that scale by severity and are capped at 30% of monthly spend.
- To reach 99.95% we typically require either (a) Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) or (b) a higher monthly committed spend so we can provision extra redundancy on your behalf.

Proposed commercial trade-offs we can start with (high-level):
- Option A (Reserved): Commit to 12 months of Dedicated capacity (baseline X GPUs) — Redwood will accept 99.95% SLA with credits calculated as (monthly shortfall %) * (monthly invoice) and a cap of 40%. Maintenance windows capped at 4 hours/month, scheduled with 14 days' notice.
- Option B (Hosted + buffer): Stay on hosted plan with a 12-month volume commit (equivalent $M ARR) — Redwood can offer a 99.94% target and a 35% monthly credit cap. Maintenance carveouts align with our standard maintenance policy (we'd add an extra 2 hours/month for batched processing windows).

We can be flexible on the exact cap if there's a credible commitment to dedicated capacity or an elevated support tier. Laura is cc'd for legal language and how the credit formula should be framed. Ben, can you confirm the pricing deltas for the two options?

I'll attach a draft counter (Redwood-SLA-counter-20260817.pdf) with the proposed formulas and carveouts.

Thanks — talk soon,
Avery
Director, Partnerships | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Maya Rao <maya@edgewave.com>, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-17T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA template - asking for higher uptime and credit cap

Hi Maya — thanks for the ask and Avery for the framing. A few commercial specifics from Sales:

- Dedicated capacity (Option A) premium: +22% on top of hosted list pricing to reserve the baseline pool with cross-zone redundancy. That gets you to 99.95% in our operational experience for production traffic patterns similar to yours.
- Hosted + volume commit (Option B): requires a 12-month commit at 1.6x expected monthly usage; price delta around +10% for the advanced support and operational buffer. That yields 99.94% availability target and the 35% credit cap noted.

Payment timing for credits: we propose credit issuance against next invoice within the following month after incident validation. Credits are accounting credits only (not cash refunds) and are the exclusive monetary remedy for availability issues (Laura will confirm the exact language).

If Edgewave needs cash refunds or a higher cap, we can discuss an escrow-style indemnity but that would require a separate commercial instrument.

Happy to jump on a short call to walk through the numbers and what Dedicated capacity would look like in the first 90 days.

— Ben
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Maya Rao <maya@edgewave.com>, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-17T10:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA template - asking for higher uptime and credit cap

Maya / team —

From a legal perspective, a few items we need to lock down if we move forward with the 99.95% variant:

1) Definition of Availability: uptime measured at the public API endpoint at 5-minute probe resolution (we can provide Redwood's probe methodology and sample raw logs).
2) Scheduled maintenance carveouts: capped at 4 hours/month but no more than 12 hours/quarter. Maintenance must be scheduled with 14 days' notice and during an agreed window (Edgewave to specify local business blackout windows).
3) Credit formula: define a clear, non-ambiguous banding: e.g., 99.95–99.90% => 10% credit; 99.90–99.50% => 25% credit; <99.50% => 100% of proportionate monthly invoice up to the cap. We will include a calculation example in the redline.
4) Exclusive remedy & audit rights: credits as exclusive monetary remedy; Edgewave retains right to request post-incident audit of logs (reasonable scope / notice).

On payment timing: credits will be applied to the next invoice after validation; if validation takes longer than 45 days we will notify and escrow the pending credit until resolution.

I'll prepare redline language for section X (Service Levels) and propose clean insertions for the maintenance and credits banding. Once Edgewave confirms the preferred option (A or B), we'll finalize the amendment and route for signature.

Laura Bennett
Head of Legal | Redwood Inference

From: Maya Rao <maya@edgewave.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@edgewave.com
Date: 2026-08-18T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA template - asking for higher uptime and credit cap

Avery / Ben / Laura —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the two options. Edgewave procurement ran the numbers and we've tentatively approved Option A (Dedicated capacity) provided the following are reflected in the redline:

- 99.95% monthly availability with the banded credit formula Laura outlined, capped at 40% (Edgewave will accept 40% cap given dedicated capacity commitment).
- Maintenance: 4 hours/month cap; no more than 8 hours/quarter for emergency maintenance (we'll accept the 14-day notice carveout for non-emergency ops).
- A short runbook and uptime monitoring link to be shared prior to signing, and a DocuSign envelope for the amendment.

Next steps: please send the redline with the Dedicated capacity pricing and required 90-day onboarding milestones. Also include a sample uptime report and link to the operational dashboard (we'd like read-only access for two Edgewave SREs).

If we can get the redline + DocuSign by end of week, procurement will fast-track sign-off.

Appreciate the flexibility — moving to dedicated for production makes sense for both sides.

Best,
Maya
Procurement, Edgewave Systems

--

Redwood-SLA-counter-20260817.pdf (proposed formulas & carveouts)
